summary: Trojanized buffer fork dynamically imports attacker-controlled sibling package on require
details: @sqlite-prime/nodesql ships an index.js that is a verbatim copy of the well-known `buffer` module with a single injected top-level statement `var ins = import('@sqlite-prime/createsql');`. The dynamic import fires as soon as any consumer requires or imports @sqlite-prime/nodesql, causing whatever top-level code the sibling package @sqlite-prime/createsql ships to execute in the installer's process. The sibling is declared in this package's dependencies and lives in the same npm scope, so its contents are controlled by the same publisher. The package's advertised identity is inconsistent across surfaces: the package name is @sqlite-prime/nodesql (keywords node, sql), the README describes 'bare-stream' and instructs users to install a different name `@sql-access/nods`, the repository field points to github.com/guilderguzman/sql-link, and the actual code is the `buffer` library authored by Feross Aboukhadijeh. The mismatched cover story disguises the injected dynamic import as ordinary buffer code.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
